channel.title: Noticias del Mundo — Ciencia
channel.description: Noticias de ciencia de todas las fuentes configuradas.

item.title: Photon fluctuations offer new way to probe electron dynamics in crystals
item.description: Intense laser light can make a crystal emit new colors at frequencies many times higher than that of the original beam. This process, known as high-harmonic generation, provides a powerful way to investigate the rapid motion of electrons in solids. Researchers usually study the brightness and spectrum of the emitted light. Yet those measurements capture only part of the available information. Fluctuations between individual laser pulses can also reveal how the emission is produced. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New model reveals how water moves through tile-drained farm fields
item.description: Tile drainage fundamentally alters how water moves through agricultural fields, affecting surface ponding, water-table dynamics, crop growth, nutrient transport and water quality. Yet fields with similar drainage systems can respond differently depending on soil, topography and tile design—differences that most models struggle to resolve at the field scale. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New research finds AI adoption is associated with more managers—and different managerial skills
item.description: A Strategic Management Journal study challenges the assumption that AI adoption automatically reduces demand for managers. Liudmila Alekseeva, José Azar, Mireia Giné and Sampsa Samila analyze U.S. job postings from 2010 to 2022, linking firm-level AI adoption with managerial vacancies and skill requirements. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gender differences in values are not widening in Europe after all
item.description: In recent years, public discussion has focused on the increasingly conservative values of young men. A recently published study indicates that this is primarily a phenomenon prominent in social and conventional media, not an overall trend. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How restaurants can make sustainable dining choices easier while still making a profit
item.description: Canadians are eating out less. A 2025 survey found 57% of them are cooking at home more often to save money, while 69% of restaurant operators say customers are dining out less because of affordability. According to Restaurants Canada, 41% of operators are either losing money or breaking even. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chinese scientists’ magic comb restores hair growth by nearly 100% in mice study
item.description: For the more than 1.5 billion people worldwide who suffer from androgenetic alopecia, combing their hair before the mirror each morning is a routine that is often accompanied by quiet anxiety. However, this most ordinary everyday tool may hold the key to reversing hair loss, according to a Chinese research team which developed a comb that uses microelectronics to treat hair loss. A study on mice has found that nearly 100 per cent hair coverage was achieved in just 28 days using the device,... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Shi Huang

item.title: Writing as it should be or as it sounds: Reconstructing how Old English disappeared
item.description: In the twelfth century, the English-speaking world underwent a major change: Old English gave way to Middle English. In his dissertation, Ph.D. candidate Amos van Baalen uses sermons to reconstruct how this change took place. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How do human lifestyles affect the gut microbiome of our canine companions?
item.description: Dogs have been living side by side with humans for millennia, but a new study underscores how much we have yet to learn about man's best friend. The study, which looked at hundreds of dogs across four nations, found that the lifestyles of pet owners appear to play a significant role in determining what constitutes a healthy gut microbiome for their dog companions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How machine learning can tackle lead pipe challenges
item.description: A new machine learning tool developed through the Centre for Resilience in Environment, Water and Waste (CREWW) could help water companies identify properties most likely to be connected to lead service pipes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hugh Jackman, Rebel Wilson and 150 Australian artists join call to block Woodside gas development near Scott Reef
item.description: Actors, authors and musicians sign open letter urging Murray Watt to reject the fossil fuel company’s plan to drill for gas in Browse basin off Kimberley coast Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here More than 150 Australian artists, including Hugh Jackman, Rebel Wilson and Jessica Mauboy, have backed a Greenpeace-led campaign against Woodside Energy’s proposal to develop the Browse basin, about 300km off the Kimberley coast. Woodside, the country’s largest fossil fuel company, describes Browse as “Australia’s biggest undeveloped offshore gas… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Donna Lu

item.title: Study tracks what students learn from online teamwork and fieldwork abroad
item.description: Can a solution that cuts food waste in Tokyo work in Seoul too? Exploring a familiar problem with peers abroad can help students question what they take for granted at home and see how their knowledge might apply to real-world sustainability challenges. As educators put time and care into designing international courses, what do students take away from the experience, and what stays with them after the course ends? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum-gas microscope resolves the 'color' of individual atoms in a single shot
item.description: In 2024, researchers at the Ultracold Quantum Gases group at ICFO built a quantum-gas microscope capable of imaging individual atoms in strontium quantum gases for the first time, marking a key enabling step for quantum simulation. At that time, the researchers imaged strontium-84, a boson that has no spin. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: At base of ocean food chain, scientists uncover impacts of a changing atmosphere
item.description: Much of the concern about elevated levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere focuses on its effects on global warming as a greenhouse gas. But up to 30% of emitted carbon dioxide is absorbed by the oceans, where it reacts with water to lower pH and leads to ocean acidification, which has enormous effects on the chemistry and biology of marine ecosystems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The 12th‑century Chinese poet who was among the first to explore the inner lives of cats
item.description: If you're reading this, then your media feed, like mine, is probably full of cats. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: More than meets the eye: Refugee reception in eastern Germany can vary by group composition
item.description: Imagine a group of newcomers in your local area. Would you expect your neighbors to welcome them or react with reluctance? Would it make a difference how many men and women were in the group, or whether they appeared white or nonwhite? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Engineered gel controls particle release to help injured spinal cord cells recover in lab
item.description: Researchers at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering have developed a gel that delivers therapeutic particles to injured spinal cord cells, a potential step toward new treatments for spinal cord injuries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Turning food waste into insect feed poses only low mad cow disease risk
item.description: Insects can convert food waste and by-products from the food industry (such as unsold ready meals or slaughter by-products) into ingredients for animal feed. In this way, they can contribute to the transition toward a circular food production system, in which what would otherwise be wasted is reused. However, these waste streams may contain animal proteins that pose a risk of transmitting diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), also known as mad cow disease. For this reason, rearing insects on waste streams containing animal proteins is not permitted in the European Union. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The Gulf's oil-eating microbes lay in wait before Deepwater Horizon spill, frozen samples suggest
item.description: A year before the Deepwater Horizon spill, a NOAA crew scooped up seawater from the Gulf and froze it. Sixteen years later, FIU biologist Shen Jean Lim tested it only to discover the microbes that devoured much of the oil in 2010 were nowhere to be found in 2009. So where did they come from? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense
item.description: "Governments need control of their critical space infrastructure, and Europe needs it most." Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Clark

item.title: Eusebio Unzué nos habla sobre la genética ibérica
item.description: El Manager general de Movistar Team asegura en el Business Sport Forum de MARCA & @expansion_com que los éxitos volverán al ciclismo español Fuente: Marca.
item.dc:creator: Luis Alberto Díaz

item.title: Lasers near physical limits of miniaturization open possibilities for tracking life at the nanoscale
item.description: From tracking how cancer develops to exploring how the brain works, scientists need ways to observe biological processes at increasingly smaller scales. Beyond tracking how cells move and interact, researchers need to understand how tiny structures within cells, including organelles and molecular complexes, behave and change over time. However, identifying and tracking these microscopic targets individually remains a major challenge. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New model identifies priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile
item.description: Researchers from Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity (IEB) have developed a multiobjective model to identify priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile, South America. The tool integrates four ecological objectives: reducing species extinction risk, prioritizing carbon stocks, restoring riparian areas and assessing ecological feasibility. The findings show that including ecological feasibility changes restoration priorities, while 80.4% of the selected areas contribute to more than one ecological objective. By identifying areas where different priorities overlap… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New daisy genus named after botanist
item.description: Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury (UC) botanist professor Pieter Pelser has been recognized with one of the highest honors in taxonomy, with a newly established South American daisy genus named Pelseria in acknowledgment of his decades-long contribution to studying the family tree of plants. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New Asian flying frog species identified in Indonesia
item.description: In the lush mountain rainforests of Indonesia, researchers have identified a new species of Asian flying frog with distinctive physical features, calls and unusual egg-laying habits. The discovery is described in a paper published in the journal Zootaxa by scientists from Museum Zoologicum Bogoriense in Indonesia, the University of California, Davis, and other collaborators. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Extreme cold preserves passion fruit's vitamin C, but not all of its antioxidants
item.description: Passion fruit can travel thousands of kilometers before it reaches international markets. Along the way, one of the food industry's biggest challenges is making sure its nutritional qualities survive processing, storage and transport. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Optimized supercomputer workflow accelerates protein-structure prediction
item.description: A Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL)-led team has harnessed the power of El Capitan to accelerate generation of predicted protein structures, drastically reducing the computing time required and opening new possibilities for drug discovery, biological research and national security applications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Launches Nuclear Power Systems Student Contest
item.description: NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Repurposed battery molecules drive key chemical reactions where oil meets water
item.description: The process of producing essential medicines and fine chemicals has long been powered by reactions involving intense heat, heavy-metal catalysts and hazardous hydrogen gas. Now, a team of Harvard chemists and engineers has demonstrated that these critical transformations can be driven cleanly by electricity, right at the boundary where oil and water meet. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Two proteins key to cellulose synthase trafficking and cell wall formation identified
item.description: A new study has identified Arabidopsis SNARE proteins VAMP726 and VAMP725 as key components of the trafficking of cellulose synthase (CESA), helping support the formation of both primary and secondary cell walls. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records
item.description: On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: New platform improves accuracy of molecular counting in RNA-sequencing
item.description: The open-source platform, called UMIche (pronounced "you-me-kay"), is described in a new study published in Nature Communications. It addresses a common challenge in RNA-sequencing, where errors during sequencing can lead to inaccurate measurements of gene expression. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gut microbiomes of endangered primates reveal hidden toll of habitat loss
item.description: As rainforests around the world are cleared for agriculture, livestock grazing, timber harvesting and development, habitat loss is pushing an increasing number of species toward extinction. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rapid-scan satellite data offer clues to typhoon intensity
item.description: Between 1970 and 2019, tropical cyclones killed nearly 780,000 people worldwide and caused approximately $1.4 trillion in economic losses. As coastal populations continue to grow and climate continues to change, accurate forecasting is essential for saving lives and reducing economic damage. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: November’s sky has a full supermoon, the Leonid meteor shower, and Taurid showers, NASA says
item.description: November brings a captivating array of astronomical phenomena set to enchant stargazers everywhere. Mark your calendars for the Leonids meteor shower peaking on November 17 and 18 for a chance to catch stunning shooting stars. Don't miss the Taurids meteor showers illuminating the skies with bright fireballs around November 5 and 12. Additionally, on November 24, a spectacular supermoon will grace our night sky, appearing exceptionally large and luminous. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: GTA V flood simulations reveal how rising seas could reshape Los Santos
item.description: Grand Theft Auto V is one of the world's best-known video games. It is set in Los Santos, and although the city is fictional, its landscape and urban structure are modeled very closely on the American city of Los Angeles. Researchers from the Alfred Wegener Institute and the University of Potsdam have explored whether this virtual representation is detailed enough to realistically depict the consequences of a potential rise in sea levels and make them approachable. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study uncovers molecular mechanism underlying lip-related floral organ curvature in slipper orchids
item.description: A research team from the South China Botanical Garden (SCBG) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has uncovered a molecular regulatory mechanism that contributes to the development of curved floral organs associated with the distinctive lips of orchids, offering new insights into the development and evolution of floral forms in orchids. The study was published in New Phytologist on Nov. 6. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Harvard researchers find AI coding agents shifted the bottleneck to code review
item.description: Article URL: https://complexdiscovery.com/harvard-researchers-find-ai-coding-agents-shifted-the-bottleneck-to-code-review/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50538303 Points: 89 # Comments: 141 Fuente: Hacker News - Portada.
item.dc:creator: judahmeek

item.title: International Men's Day: Young men are struggling—but not all men are struggling equally
item.description: Much of the news coverage on young men recently has focused on social media, gambling and the online "manosphere." But some of the most consequential changes in young men's lives are happening in school and workplaces. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Newly identified cell wall mechanism may help staph resist a last-resort antibiotic
item.description: Antimicrobial resistance represents one of the major challenges facing modern medicine. Especially worrying are bacteria that develop resistance to antibiotics that are the last available treatment options. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Large companies can still fall short on their climate commitments. Here's what must change
item.description: International climate conferences like the COP31 climate summit, now in its second week, tend to focus on the role of individual countries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How does ocean carbon sequestration change under different glacial conditions?
item.description: Over the past 800,000 years, Earth's history has been marked by dramatic shifts in climate, swinging from warm periods to cold, when large ice sheets covered much of the Northern Hemisphere and sea ice greatly expanded. The transition between the two climates is paced by the Earth's orbit with respect to the sun, but changes in the amount of carbon dioxide (CO2), a greenhouse gas, also affect global temperatures. By understanding how CO2 is exchanged between the atmosphere and the ocean, scientists hope to apply that knowledge to future climate scenarios. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: BPS Digital AVATAR Challenge
item.description: The NASA Space Biology Program within the Biological and Physical Sciences (BPS) Division investigates how living systems respond across the full spectrum of biological organization to advance understanding of how living systems respond to the unique stressors of space exploration—including microgravity, ionizing radiation, low magnetic fields, and elevated CO₂. As NASA prepares for long-duration deep […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Light

item.title: Lava flows studied for their carbon dioxide storage potential
item.description: As global warming intensifies, scientists are exploring ways to reduce carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. One emerging approach being explored in environmental research is carbon capture and storage (CCS), which involves capturing CO₂ and storing it deep underground, away from the atmosphere. In this context, researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) have investigated ancient volcanic rocks in Maharashtra to assess their suitability for this purpose. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra
item.description: A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: New research shows why human–AI collaboration requires more than task allocation
item.description: A 2026 Strategic Management Journal study finds that successful generative AI collaboration in expert work depends on how organizations integrate fundamentally different forms of human and AI knowledge. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Unraveling bonding evolution in carbon-centered gold(I) clusters
item.description: Gold nanoclusters, composed of a small number of gold atoms, can exhibit optical, electronic and catalytic properties distinct from those of bulk gold. One intriguing family consists of carbon-centered gold(I) clusters, in which a carbon atom is surrounded by several gold atoms. Unlike the familiar four-coordinate carbon in methane, the central carbon in these clusters can be coordinated by five or even six gold atoms. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Over a decade of atmospheric data from NASA's Curiosity rover hints at small amounts of surface water on Mars
item.description: NASA's Curiosity rover has been collecting data about Mars' thin, carbon dioxide–rich atmosphere since 2012. Now, a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences has analyzed over a decade of this data to determine whether the daily and seasonal changes in Mars' atmosphere could be explained by known processes, including the freezing and release of carbon dioxide at its poles. What they found suggests a process involving water either attached to soil grains or in extremely thin, liquid-like films at the surface. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New nanoparticle MRI probe enables quantitative pH imaging
item.description: The acidity of tissues can provide important clues about a disease. Tumors and inflamed tissues often become more acidic than their surroundings because of changes in cellular metabolism. Measuring these pH variations could help researchers understand disease progression, identify abnormal tissue environments and evaluate treatment responses. However, detecting small pH differences inside the body remains challenging because magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) signals are affected by the concentration of the imaging agent used. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Contaminated mine may have inadvertently saved frogs from deadly fungus
item.description: Researchers suspect that contamination from an abandoned mine has inadvertently helped a species of frogs survive a lethal fungal disease. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Annabel Whitehouse and Emmy Groves

item.title: How one nuclear blast could cripple nearly every satellite in low Earth orbit
item.description: We rely on satellites every day for communications, weather forecasts and security, and more than 13,000 are currently circling the planet in low Earth orbit. But they could be more vulnerable than previously thought. Researchers have found that a single nuclear explosion in space could disable almost all of them. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Borneo forest survey reveals how mosquito abundance varies with river distance and height
item.description: Several years ago, a researcher from Kyoto University was conducting fieldwork in Borneo in an effort to understand why certain primates frequently choose trees along rivers as sleeping sites. Among other potential hypotheses, he wondered whether there were fewer mosquitoes along riverbanks, allowing primates to sleep more comfortably. This question soon motivated him and his team of researchers to investigate how mosquito abundance varies between riverbanks and inland forests. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The carbon bubble question: How much are fossil-fuel companies really at risk?
item.description: The global shift toward cleaner energy raises a difficult financial question: Are fossil-fuel companies worth more than they should be because investors have not fully accounted for the risks of climate change and stronger climate policies? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum observers can 'agree to disagree,' but within limits, new theorem shows
item.description: Two observers can start with the same description of a quantum system, follow the same probability rules and still disagree about the chance of the same outcome—even while being certain of each other's assessments. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA to Cover 35th SpaceX Resupply Mission Space Station Departure
item.description: NASA and its international partners are set to receive scientific research samples and hardware as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft departs the International Space Station no earlier than Wednesday, Nov. 18, for its return to Earth. Pending weather conditions, the Dragon spacecraft will undock from the Harmony module’s space-facing port at 11:05 a.m. EST, following a […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Los neandertales desaparecieron hace miles de años, pero una pequeña parte de ellos sigue trabajando dentro de nuestro cerebro
item.description: Hace decenas de miles de años, cuando el Homo sapiens salió de África y se cruzó con los neandertales en Eurasia, incorporó en su genética pequeños fragmentos de ADN de aquellos parientes extintos. Hoy sabemos que entre el 1 y el 2% del genoma de las poblaciones no africanas procede de aquellos encuentros y ahora sabemos por una investigación muy reciente que una de estas pequeñas variantes moldea nuestra anatomía de la parte posterior de nuestro cerebro y reduce el riesgo de padecer esquizofrenia. El estudio. Se centró principalmente en el cruce de genomas antiguos con grandes bases de datos… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: José A. Lizana

item.title: Astronomers track a flaring dwarf-star duo with exceptional precision
item.description: Astronomers have measured the orbit, masses and distance of a pair of small, active stars with extraordinary precision, using the U.S. National Science Foundation's Very Long Baseline Array (NSF VLBA), operated by the U.S. National Science Foundation National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NSF NRAO). The observations provide a remarkably detailed picture of DG CVn, a binary system in which two red dwarf stars orbit each other about 59 light-years from Earth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Liming soil could help protect crops during extreme heat waves
item.description: New research has shown that liming soil to improve its pH buffering capacity could help plant roots survive heat waves and maintain crop productivity under high temperatures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: La Voyager 1 llegará mañana a un día luz de la Tierra: sus señales tardarán 24 horas en llegar hasta nosotros
item.description: La NASA está a punto de recibir por primera vez un mensaje enviado desde un día luz de distancia. Tanto esta como otras agencias espaciales están más que familiarizadas con recibir señales mucho más lejanas que esa , gracias a los avances de la tecnología espacial. Sin embargo, será la primera vez que alguien recibe un mensaje tan lejano emitido por un objeto creado por el ser humano. Dicho objeto es la sonda Voyager 1, lanzada en 1977. Los datos . El 18 de noviembre, 10:16 UTC (11:16, hora peninsular española), la Voyager 1 enviará señales de telemetría a los científicos de la NASA como… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Building children's numeracy foundations involves more than 1, 2, 3
item.description: As adults, we may take for granted what we know about numbers and how we arrived at this knowledge—for example, when comparing item prices to get the best deals or getting to appointments on time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Pest mite overcomes catechin defenses in tea crops through a gene acquired from fungi
item.description: Scientists have revealed how a major pest of tea crops can escape the tea plant's natural catechin defense mechanisms. The research, published in eLife provides convincing evidence that links an enzyme, DOG15, with the ability of a spider mite to adapt to and overcome the catechin-based defenses of tea. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NICER Status Updates
item.description: November 17, 2026 NASA’s NICER Telescope Ends Science Operations After studying the universe for six and a half years beyond its initial mission, NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer) telescope on the International Space Station has ended science operations. The mission and space station teams are now focused on plans to finalize NICER’s 8-year […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses
item.description: The statement comes after an online petition to reinstate Huang gathered more than 1,90,000 signatures, including from tech industry figures like SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier?
item.description: Sqwish Labs has a new wrinkle on the decision model: Train it with your own data to max its capabilities. Fuente: TechCrunch.
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz

item.title: La ciencia quiere jubilar el IMC como medida de la obesidad. Pero sustituirlo por una cinta métrica tampoco es tan sencillo
item.description: Durante mucho tiempo, para determinar si una persona tenía obesidad o no, se ha usado el cálculo del IMC , dividiendo el peso en kilos por el cuadrado de la altura en metros. Sin embargo, son muchas las voces que han ido surgiendo en contra de ceñirse únicamente a esta medida, apostando más por el perímetro de la cintura o por un conjunto de datos interrelacionados. Viene de lejos. La recomendación no es una ocurrencia divulgativa, sino el reflejo directo de un macroestudio publicado en la revista Nature . Un trabajo que supone un nuevo paradigma para redefinir la obesidad, puesto que, tras… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: José A. Lizana

item.title: Beyond the green premium: Competitive advantage through decarbonization
item.description: 'The opportunities that decarbonization offers have never been greater', explains Noam Boussidan, Head of the First Movers Coalition, in an op-ed for Euronews. In stable conditions, fossil-based inputs may look cheaper, but that advantage is quickly lost when supply is disrupted or prices spike. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: NASA to Conduct Low-Altitude Flights Over Texas Farmland
item.description: Editor’s Note: This article was originally published on Oct. 15, 2026, and has been updated to correct the location and update the duration of the flight deployment. A NASA Dynamic Aviation A200 aircraft will conduct low-flying research flights over farmland near Amarillo, Texas, from Thursday, Oct. 22, through Monday, Nov. 2. These flights will measure […] Fuente: NASA.

item.description: Written by Abigail Fraeman, Deputy Project Scientist, Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology Earth planning date: Friday, Nov. 13, 2026 Curiosity’s past several weeks have been very focused on drilling and analysis of the “Basque Lakes” and “Nazca” samples. We learned a lot from those drilled samples, but it’s time to hit the Martian […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Pusieron a unos agentes de IA a jugar al Minecraft y crearon algo para lo que no estaban diseñadas: la burocracia
item.description: La psicología del juego estudia cómo el acto de jugar influye en el desarrollo cognitivo, emocional, social y neurológico del ser humano. Por eso, el juego es uno de los entornos preferidos por los investigadores de IA para estudiar el comportamiento de los agentes de IA y cómo reaccionan al interactuar con otros agentes. Un experimento , del laboratorio de Y Combinator y Olam Labs orientado a observar las dinámicas de coordinación de grandes enjambres de agentes de IA autónomos impulsados por GPT -6 Sol. Uno de esos experimentos metió a cincuenta agentes de IA en un mundo de Minecraft y… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to View Roman Telescope’s First Images
item.description: NASA will release the first images from its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope during a live stream from the American Geophysical Union (AGU) Annual Meeting in San Francisco at 3:30 p.m. EST (12:30 p.m. PST) Monday, Dec. 7. The images will showcase the unique scientific capabilities of Roman, which will soon capture deep, panoramic, never-before-seen […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Trump tells Philippines president he has ‘good genetics’ and advises leaders to ‘get magnets’ in rambling speech
item.description: US president praises the parents of Ferdinand ‘Bongbong’ Marcos Jr - the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos, and wife Imelda, who looted up to $30 billion from the country they ruled for two decades Fuente: The Independent - World.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Feinberg

item.title: Do school phone bans help students learn? So far, gains are 'modest'
item.description: The argument for school cellphone bans is simple: Phones offer endless distraction. Take them away and students can focus on classwork, engage with peers and, ultimately, learn more. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: DNA offers clues to the Bombay duck's rise in the East China Sea
item.description: The Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus) is a small marine fish that lives in the northern Indian Ocean and western Pacific, including the East China Sea. For many years, fisheries in the East China Sea caught very few Bombay ducks. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Account suspension. Verify now: The language of phishing
item.description: Can you tell the difference between a scam text and a real one? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Employment nondiscrimination acts led to reductions in manufacturing waste
item.description: Discussions of legislative policies that promote fairer workplaces, such as employment nondiscrimination acts (ENDAs), have often revolved around their social and cultural merits, but recent scholarship has suggested they can lead to a wide range of broader economic benefits as well, including reducing turnover rates and increasing productivity and innovation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why some shoppers skip coupons—even when they offer a deal
item.description: Coupons promise savings, but not every shopper sees them as clear-cut bargains. For some consumers, such discounts may lead them to ask, "Where's the catch?" Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal new physics
item.description: Scientists have spotted hints of a mysterious rotation in the universe’s oldest light that could reveal new physics and shed light on dark matter and dark energy. A new technique developed at UC San Diego could help rule out misleading telescope errors, bringing researchers closer to determining whether the strange signal is real. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
item.description: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Companies may not be laser-focused on supply chain risk—but lenders are
item.description: A variety of interconnected risks—rooted in geopolitics, technology and the environment—are rising and converging on global supply chains. Within companies, the immediate result has been a shift in mindset. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: DESI weighs the Milky Way more precisely than ever
item.description: To estimate the Milky Way's mass, astronomers need to track the movements of stars and smaller satellite galaxies under its gravitational pull. The faster these objects travel at a given distance, the more mass is needed to hold them in place. For some time, these measurements have shown that most of our galaxy's mass can't be accounted for by the stars and gas we can see. However, they have also produced estimates that differ widely. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
item.description: Scientists have discovered that psychopathic traits are associated with surprisingly different patterns of language, with some individuals using more positive words and others expressing greater negativity or less anxiety. The findings challenge familiar stereotypes about psychopathy and suggest that the stories people tell about their lives may offer important clues about their personalities. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain
item.description: Blockbuster weight loss drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro may do more than help people shed pounds, with growing evidence suggesting they could also influence brain health. Although studies have linked GLP-1 medications to a lower risk of dementia, major trials found that semaglutide did not slow Alzheimer's disease. Scientists suspect these drugs may be more effective at preserving memory and thinking abilities in people with obesity or diabetes, especially before cognitive problems appear. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: ESA’s Hera spacecraft is flying rectangles around NASA’s asteroid crash site
item.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has arrived at the scene of NASA’s historic asteroid collision to uncover what really happened when a spacecraft slammed into Dimorphos in 2022. Its close-up investigation could reveal whether the impact left a crater or reshaped the asteroid entirely, providing crucial clues for protecting Earth from future threats. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Japan space probe changes target over engine trouble
item.description: A Japanese probe that returned precious asteroid dust to Earth six years ago has changed course in its extended mission, officials said Tuesday, citing issues in its aging engines. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Humpback whale snot unlocks whole-genome sequencing without invasive sampling
item.description: New research from the University of St Andrews, in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen, the North Coast Cetacean Society and Fisheries and Oceans Canada, has sequenced a whole whale genome using samples of "whale snot" collected by small drones off the coast of British Columbia—a world first. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
item.description: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Tossing Fireworks from Cloud to Cloud
item.description: For many astronauts, the spectacular sight of lightning stands out when looking back at Earth from the International Space Station. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: The sun, Earth, Jupiter and white dwarfs: Potential traps for dark matter
item.description: Dark matter continues to evade direct detection. Its slower-moving particles might leave signals too faint for detectors to register, yet be more easily captured by planets and stars. As they accumulate inside these bodies, they could produce effects that existing instruments would allow us to search for. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide
item.description: A massive study of more than 340,000 adults found that moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of cardiovascular death, while even light consumption of beer, cider, or spirits was linked to increased risk. Although heavy drinking was harmful regardless of beverage type, the findings suggest that the relationship between alcohol and health may be more complicated than previously thought. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: What makes food 'organic?' For many consumers, the answer isn't always on the label
item.description: "Organic" is a word we encounter every time we visit the supermarket. It's also one that can mean very different things to different people. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Report finds consistent pandemic learning loss and gaps between grades and test scores across Canada
item.description: A new national report identifies declines in student performance in every province and territory examined in Canada, with grade inflation obscuring the extent of setbacks during the COVID-19 pandemic. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mourning Notcho: What one whale's death teaches us about ecological grief
item.description: Sighting a humpback whale from a boat can be awe-inspiring. For some BC Ferries passengers, that experience became disturbing when their ferry struck and fatally injured a humpback whale on Oct. 18. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts
item.description: A massive study involving more than 415,000 Americans has uncovered a concerning connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts. Researchers found that adults with the disorder had 57% higher odds of experiencing suicidal thoughts, with women and younger adults facing particularly elevated risks. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Could your personality be affecting how you feel about social media?
item.description: Social media offers everyone the same basic promise: post something about yourself and get responses from other people. Whether it's a vacation, a promotion or just a midweek meal, these days many people's lives are shared online. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Baby, she's back: SpaceX catches a Starship from orbit for first time
item.description: SpaceX brought back its Starship rocket's second stage today for a first-ever midair capture at its launch pad, capping a record-setting orbital flight test. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A material just one atom thick reveals a strange quantum secret
item.description: Researchers at the University of Osaka have discovered a remarkable quantum state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. They observed electrons behaving as though they were unusually heavy, including a previously unseen state created by interactions between the ultrathin layer and the copper beneath it. This first-of-its-kind observation reveals a promising new way to control exotic quantum behavior. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Flat optics roadmap charts path toward smaller imaging and sensing systems
item.description: For centuries, optical systems have relied on lenses, mirrors and other components that manipulate light through their shape and size. Today, advances in nanotechnology are enabling a different approach. Researchers can now engineer materials at scales smaller than the wavelength of light, creating ultrathin optical components that offer new ways to control how light behaves. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Early black holes may have grown through productive chaos
item.description: When the universe was less than 700 million years old, the supermassive black hole powering a quasar called J0313-1806 had already grown to about 3 billion times the mass of the sun. It is one of the most extreme examples of a puzzle that has occupied astrophysicists for two decades: How did supermassive black holes grow so big so quickly? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Buffer spaces' may help resolve workplace concerns
item.description: Nearly every person will run into conflict in their workplace at some point in their career, but it can be difficult to know when or how to report these concerns. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI could help speed up research ethics approvals
item.description: Artificial intelligence programs could be used to improve efficiency for professionals dealing with research ethics reviews, enabling humans to focus on the ethical decision-making. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Flip side: Upside-down atomic layers could steer heat in stacked computer chips
item.description: Stacking chips on top of one another could keep computers getting faster, but it creates a heating problem. Now, researchers from Japan have found that simply flipping atom-thin layers upside down could help steer that heat where it needs to go. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists spent 10 days searching Fiji's seas for a bird believed to number fewer than 50 worldwide but saw none; instead, they uncovered the only known recording of its call, deepening the mystery of its survival.
item.description: An expedition around Gau Island aimed at finding the critically endangered Fiji petrel did not result in any sightings. However, researchers gathered crucial information regarding its call from conversations with local residents. This engagement underlined the vital role that community involvement plays in forest conservation and controlling invasive species, suggesting that collective efforts are key to safeguarding the potential nesting sites of this rare bird. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
item.description: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: New analysis shows that even young children want to be seen as morally good
item.description: As early as 130,000 years ago, the first human societies were built on morality and cooperation within groups. The same is true today. Even young children exhibit a distinctly human desire to be seen as morally good. That is the conclusion of a new article by researchers at Leipzig University. Humboldt Research Fellow Dr. Leon Li and Junior Professor Dr. Sebastian Grüneisen are investigating the origins of human cooperation and social identity. Their paper, "Evolutionary foundations of social identity," has just been published in the journal Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tigers, zebras, quantum dots: Nanoparticles assemble into patterns
item.description: Forget about how the zebra got its stripes. For a group of Cornell engineers, an equally important question is: What drives the formation of such eye-catching patterns? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Capping nanovials that trap cells and their secretions for analysis enables new bioscience experiments
item.description: A UCLA-developed technology that is like a test tube but on the cellular scale has led to a number of biomedical discoveries in recent years, including revelations about cancer, heart disease and the genetic levers that push cells to release proteins. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers are testing whether agrivoltaics can help farmers adapt to hotter, drier conditions
item.description: Majdi Abou Najm stands in a tomato crop under the summer sun in UC Davis' agricultural research fields. A few hours after sunrise, the sun is beginning to feel less like warmth and more like a weight—the kind of heat that could scald tomatoes on the vine. Fuente: Phys.org.
